question.problem:
Let $V=C[0,1],$ the vector space of functions that are continuous over $[0,1].$ Given that the inner product on $V$ is defined as 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{1}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t,
$$

find the orthogonal projection of $f(t)=12({t}^{2}-t)$ onto the subspace spanned by $g(t)=t-1.$

current_example.problem:
Let $V = \Bbb R_1[t],$ the vector space of polynomials of degree at most $1$ with real coefficients. Given that the inner product on $V$ is defined as 

$$
\langle p(t),q(t) \rangle = p(0)q(0)+p(1)q(1),
$$

find the orthogonal projection of $p(t)=-5t-3$ onto the subspace spanned by the polynomial $q(t) =t-1.$
current_example.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $p(t)$ onto $\textrm{Span}\{ q(t) \}$ is given by

$$
\textrm{proj}_{q(t)}\,p(t) 
= \dfrac{\langle{p(t),q(t)}\rangle}{\langle{q(t),q(t)}\rangle}\,q(t).
$$

 

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨p(t),q(t)⟩ & =p(0)q(0)+p(1)q(1) \\  & =(-5t-3){|}_{0}\cdot (t-1){|}_{0}+(-5t-3){|}_{1}\cdot (t-1){|}_{1} \\  & =(-3)\cdot (-1)+(-8)\cdot 0 \\  & =3+0 \\  & =3,\end{aligned}
$$

 

and

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨q(t),q(t)⟩ & =q(0)q(0)+q(1)q(1) \\  & =(t-1){|}_{0}\cdot (t-1){|}_{0}+(t-1){|}_{1}\cdot (t-1){|}_{1} \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-1)+0\cdot 0 \\  & =1+0 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the projection is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{q(t)}\,p(t) & =\frac{⟨p(t),q(t)⟩}{⟨q(t),q(t)⟩}\,q(t) \\  & =\frac{3}{1}\cdot (t-1) \\  & =3(t-1).\end{aligned}
$$
